prompt: A content site ships 400 KB of JavaScript to hydrate pages that only have a search box and a newsletter form as interactive parts.
tells: only have a search box and a newsletter form
why: Ship static HTML and hydrate just the two widgets.
trap: Splitting the bundle still hydrates the whole page.

prompt: A pricing page is static except for a currency switcher, which should be the only part that loads JavaScript.
tells: static except for a currency switcher
the only part that loads JavaScript
why: That's an island: one interactive component in a static page.
trap: Code splitting still loads the page's framework runtime.

prompt: A comments widget at the bottom of articles should only hydrate when the reader scrolls near it.
tells: only hydrate when the reader scrolls near it
why: Islands can hydrate on visibility, saving work for readers who never scroll.
trap: Virtualization is about long lists, not one widget.

prompt: Lighthouse shows high total blocking time from hydrating a large, mostly static page.
tells: high total blocking time from hydrating
why: Hydrate less: only the interactive islands.
trap: A worker can't hydrate DOM; it's the amount of hydration.

prompt: A product page is static content except for an "Add to cart" button and a cart badge in the header.
why: Hydrate just the button and the badge as islands.
trap: Optimistic UI may live inside them, but the architecture is islands.

prompt: A blog built with Astro ships zero JavaScript by default and only hydrates components marked client:load.
trap: Static generation explains the HTML; islands explain the JS.

prompt: An article has one interactive chart in the middle, and the rest is text that never changes.
tells: the rest is text that never changes
why: Make the chart an island and keep the article static.
trap: Hydrating the whole article for one chart is waste.

prompt: A docs site uses a React search widget and a Svelte playground on otherwise static pages, each hydrating independently.
tells: React search widget and a Svelte playground
why: Islands are independent, so they can even use different frameworks.
trap: It's not splitting one app; they are separate apps.
